subject: political_science
question_text: Write true or false against each of these statements:

parts.part_text: A Bill of Rights lays down the rights enjoyed by the people of a country.
A Bill of Rights protects the liberties of an individual.
Every country of the world has a Bill of Rights.
The Constitution guarantees remedy against violation of Rights.

difficulty_reasoning: Direct recall of true or false statements.

subject: political_science
question_text: Read the following situations. Which Fundamental Right is being used or violated in each case and how?

parts.part_text: Overweight male cabin crew are allowed to get promotion in the national airlines but their women colleagues who gain weight are penalised.
parts.answer_text: The Right being violated is the Right to equality of opportunity in employment.

parts.part_text: A director makes a documentary film that criticises the policies of the government.
parts.answer_text: The Right being used is the Freedom of speech and expression.

parts.part_text: People displaced by a big dam take out a rally demanding rehabilitation.
parts.answer_text: The Right being used is the Freedom of expression and Freedom to assemble peacefully.

parts.part_text: Andhra society runs Telugu medium schools outside Andhra Pradesh.
parts.answer_text: The Right being used is the Cultural right to represent and protect one's own language and culture.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of Fundamental Rights and application to scenarios.

subject: political_science
question_text: Which of the following is the best description of Fundamental Rights?
answer_text: The rights given and protected by the Constitution.
final_answer: Therefore, the best description of Fundamental Rights is that they are the rights given and protected by the Constitution.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the concept of Fundamental Rights.

subject: political_science
question_text: An activist working among the poor says that the poor don't need Fundamental Rights. What they need are Directive Principles to be made legally binding. Do you agree with this? Give your reasons.
answer_text: No, I do not agree with this statement. Fundamental Rights cannot be denied to any section of the society and this is applicable to the poorer sections as well. While implementation of directive principles is required for improving the condition of the poor, fundamental rights are universal as they ensure dignity to every citizen and form the basis for equality among people. Certain rights like right to constitutional remedy are important to secure protection for the poorest and weakest sections of the society from the arbitrary action of the state. Enforcement of directive principles is important for ensuring social, economic and political justice. However, freedom of expression is still required to raise voice against any form of discrimination or injustice.
final_answer: Therefore, Fundamental Rights are essential for ensuring dignity and equality for all citizens, including the poor.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the importance of Fundamental Rights versus Directive Principles.

subject: political_science
question_text: Several reports show that caste groups previously associated with scavenging are forced to continue in this job. Those in positions of authority refuse to give them any other job. Their children are discouraged from pursuing education. Which of their Fundamental Rights are being violated in this instance?
answer_text: Fundamental right against exploitation, such as prohibition of forced labour, is violated in this situation by forcing certain castes to continue in the same job that is associated with their caste. Right to practice any profession is violated as they are refused any other jobs by the authorities. Prohibition of employment of children in hazardous jobs is also violated in this instance.
final_answer: Thus, multiple Fundamental Rights are being violated, including the right against exploitation and the right to practice any profession.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of specific Fundamental Rights and their application.

subject: political_science
question_text: A petition by a human rights group drew attention of the court to the condition of starvation and hunger in the country. Over five crore tonnes of food grains was stored in the godowns of the Food Corporation of India. Research shows that a large number of ration cardholders do not know about the quantity of food grains they can purchase from fair price shops. It requested the court to order the government to improve its public distribution system. a. Which different rights does this case involve? How are these rights interlinked? b. Should these rights form part of the right to life?

parts.part_text: Which different rights does this case involve? How are these rights interlinked?
parts.answer_text: The case involves the use of Right to speech and expression and constitutional remedy. These rights were used by the human rights group to inform the court about the prevailing condition of hunger and starvation, thus requesting the court to order the government to improve public distribution system. The right to life of people is also invoked to address hunger and starvation. These rights are interlinked as freedom of speech provides the basis for constitutional remedies.
parts.final_answer: Thus, the rights to speech, constitutional remedy, and the right to life are interlinked in addressing hunger.

parts.part_text: Should these rights form part of the right to life?
parts.answer_text: Yes, these rights should form part of the right to life as they are necessary for the sustenance of people.
parts.final_answer: Therefore, these rights are essential for ensuring the right to life.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the interlinking of rights and their implications on life.

subject: Political Science
question_text: Which of the Fundamental Rights is in your opinion the most important right? Summarise its provisions and give arguments to show why it is most important.
answer_text: The right to constitutional remedies is the most important right. The provisions of this right include the right to move the courts for issuance of writs. The Supreme Court and High Courts can issue directives to the government for the implementation of rights. The special orders issued by courts for enforcement of rights are as follows: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari. This right safeguards the other fundamental rights and ensures their realization.
final_answer: Therefore, the Right to Constitutional Remedies is crucial as it protects and enforces all other fundamental rights.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of fundamental rights and their implications.
